title: MD SB141: Election Law - Election Misinformation, Election Disinformation, and Deepfakes

obligations: The State Board shall maintain a portal on its website for the public to report election misinformation and election disinformation (Sec. 2, 110(b)(1))

The State Board shall conduct a periodic review of material submitted through the portal and, to the extent necessary, issue corrective information or refer submissions to the State Prosecutor (Sec. 2, 110(b)(2))

If the State Administrator receives a credible report that election misinformation or election disinformation, including a deepfake, has been or is being communicated, disseminated, or distributed, the State Administrator shall communicate, disseminate, or distribute to the public accurate information to correct it (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)1)

The State Administrator may seek an injunction in accordance with the Maryland Rules for the removal of election misinformation or election disinformation from any online platform (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)2)

The State Administrator may issue a subpoena in accordance with the Federal Stored Communications Act, if applicable, for records related to the dissemination or distribution of election misinformation or disinformation, including information related to the targeted audience (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)3)

The State Board, in consultation with the State Administrator, may file a civil action in a court of competent jurisdiction within the State against a person, campaign, political action committee, or other legal entity if the State Board finds that the entity created, used, or disseminated election disinformation or, with reckless disregard, election misinformation, and incurs costs to communicate accurate information to correct it (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii))
The State Board may seek damages, court costs, and attorney's fees in a civil action filed under Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii) (Sec. 2, 110(c)(3)(i))

A court may award damages, court costs, or attorney's fees in a civil action filed under Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii) only based on a showing by clear and convincing evidence that the person, campaign, political action committee, or other legal entity created, used, or disseminated election disinformation or, with reckless disregard, election misinformation (Sec. 2, 110(c)(4))
prohibitions: The State Administrator may not seek an injunction against an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. § 230, for content disseminated by another person through the interactive computer service (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(ii))

The State Board may not file a civil action against a person exempt from the requirements of § 16, 905 of this article or a person who seeks to detect, report, prevent, investigate, respond to, or prosecute persons responsible for security breaches, identity theft, fraud, harassment, or other malicious or illegal activity (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(i))
The State Board may not seek damages, court costs, or attorney's fees in a civil action against a person exempt from the requirements of § 16, 905 of this article (Sec. 2, 110(c)(3)(ii))

A person may not knowingly or with reckless disregard create, use, or disseminate a deepfake to produce materially false information if the person has the intent to use the deepfake to impede, influence, prevent, or attempt to impede, influence, or prevent a voter's decision to cast a ballot; misrepresent facts relating to voter registration, voting methods, election results, electoral processes, or official duties of an election official; induce or attempt to induce another individual to sign or not sign a petition for a question to appear on a ballot; or influence or attempt to influence a voter's decision whether to vote for or against a candidate or ballot issue, and the creation, use, or dissemination results, or has the intent to result, in harm to a voter, potential voter, or petition (Sec. 16, 905(c))

Passed 2026-05-12. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Requires the State Administrator of Elections to correct election misinformation and disinformation, authorizes injunctions and subpoenas, allows the State Board of Elections to sue for damages, and makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly or recklessly create, use, or disseminate certain election-related deepfakes.

Who it applies to

  • State Administrator of Elections
  • State Board of Elections
  • persons who create, use, or disseminate deepfakes
  • campaigns, political action committees, and other legal entities
  • online platforms from which election misinformation or disinformation may be removed
  • broadcasters, websites, and periodicals that may qualify for exemptions

Effective date

June 1, 2026

Key definitions

  • Election disinformation: incorrect or misleading information regarding the time, place, or manner of an election, election results, or voting rights in the State that is knowingly and deliberately disseminated (Sec. 2, 110(a)(2))
  • Election misinformation: incorrect or misleading information regarding the time, place, or manner of an election, election results, or voting rights in the State (Sec. 2, 110(a)(3))
  • Deepfake: an image, an audio recording, or a video recording that has been intentionally created or manipulated with the use of generative artificial intelligence or other digital technology to create a realistic but false depiction of a person that an ordinary person would conclude is an actual visual or audio representation of the person depicted (Sec. 16, 905(a)(2))
  • Influence: has the meaning stated in § 16, 201 of this title (Sec. 16, 905(a)(3))

Obligations

  • The State Board shall maintain a portal on its website for the public to report election misinformation and election disinformation (Sec. 2, 110(b)(1))
  • The State Board shall conduct a periodic review of material submitted through the portal and, to the extent necessary, issue corrective information or refer submissions to the State Prosecutor (Sec. 2, 110(b)(2))
  • If the State Administrator receives a credible report that election misinformation or election disinformation, including a deepfake, has been or is being communicated, disseminated, or distributed, the State Administrator shall communicate, disseminate, or distribute to the public accurate information to correct it (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)1)
  • The State Administrator may seek an injunction in accordance with the Maryland Rules for the removal of election misinformation or election disinformation from any online platform (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)2)
  • The State Administrator may issue a subpoena in accordance with the Federal Stored Communications Act, if applicable, for records related to the dissemination or distribution of election misinformation or disinformation, including information related to the targeted audience (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)3)
  • The State Board, in consultation with the State Administrator, may file a civil action in a court of competent jurisdiction within the State against a person, campaign, political action committee, or other legal entity if the State Board finds that the entity created, used, or disseminated election disinformation or, with reckless disregard, election misinformation, and incurs costs to communicate accurate information to correct it (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii))
  • The State Board may seek damages, court costs, and attorney's fees in a civil action filed under Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii) (Sec. 2, 110(c)(3)(i))
  • A court may award damages, court costs, or attorney's fees in a civil action filed under Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii) only based on a showing by clear and convincing evidence that the person, campaign, political action committee, or other legal entity created, used, or disseminated election disinformation or, with reckless disregard, election misinformation (Sec. 2, 110(c)(4))

Prohibitions

  • The State Administrator may not seek an injunction against an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. § 230, for content disseminated by another person through the interactive computer service (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(ii))
  • The State Board may not file a civil action against a person exempt from the requirements of § 16, 905 of this article or a person who seeks to detect, report, prevent, investigate, respond to, or prosecute persons responsible for security breaches, identity theft, fraud, harassment, or other malicious or illegal activity (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(i))
  • The State Board may not seek damages, court costs, or attorney's fees in a civil action against a person exempt from the requirements of § 16, 905 of this article (Sec. 2, 110(c)(3)(ii))
  • A person may not knowingly or with reckless disregard create, use, or disseminate a deepfake to produce materially false information if the person has the intent to use the deepfake to impede, influence, prevent, or attempt to impede, influence, or prevent a voter's decision to cast a ballot; misrepresent facts relating to voter registration, voting methods, election results, electoral processes, or official duties of an election official; induce or attempt to induce another individual to sign or not sign a petition for a question to appear on a ballot; or influence or attempt to influence a voter's decision whether to vote for or against a candidate or ballot issue, and the creation, use, or dissemination results, or has the intent to result, in harm to a voter, potential voter, or petition (Sec. 16, 905(c))

Penalties and enforcement

The State Administrator may seek an injunction for removal of election misinformation or disinformation from an online platform and may issue a subpoena for records (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)2, 3). The State Board may file a civil action and seek damages, court costs, and attorney's fees; a court may award these only on clear and convincing evidence (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii), (3), (4)). A person who violates Sec. 16, 905(c) is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction is subject to a fine of not more than $5,000 or imprisonment for not more than 5 years or both (Sec. 16, 905(d)). The text does not state a private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying generative AI or other digital technology to create or manipulate images, audio, or video of a person must ensure it does not knowingly or with reckless disregard create, use, or disseminate a deepfake with the prohibited intents and resulting or intended harm (Sec. 16, 905(c))
  • If such a deepfake is reported as election misinformation or disinformation, the State Administrator must correct it publicly and may seek an injunction to remove it from an online platform or issue a subpoena for records, including targeted audience information (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)1, 2, 3)
  • The State Board may sue the deploying organisation, campaign, PAC, or legal entity for damages, court costs, and attorney's fees if it incurs costs to correct the misinformation or disinformation (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii), (3)(i))
  • Exemptions exist for satire or parody, certain broadcasters with disclosure or good faith efforts, news publications with clear statements, and online publishers or service providers with 47 U.S.C. § 230 immunity (Sec. 16, 905(b)(1), (4))
  • Organisations should implement content review, provenance tracking, and disclosure mechanisms to avoid criminal liability and civil exposure (Sec. 16, 905(c), (d); Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii))

Notable exemptions

  • A deepfake that is satire or parody (Sec. 16, 905(b)(1))
  • A radio or television broadcasting station, including a cable or satellite television operator, programmer, or producer, or an affiliate, that broadcasts a deceptive and fraudulent deepfake if the broadcast is required by federal law requiring broadcasters to air advertisements from legally qualified candidates; or the broadcast is part of a bona fide newscast, news interview, news documentary, or on-the-spot coverage of bona fide news events and clearly identifies to the audience that the deepfake may contain deceptive audio or visual media; or the broadcaster has been paid to broadcast the deepfake and made a good faith effort to establish that it is not a deceptive and fraudulent deepfake (Sec. 16, 905(b)(2))
  • A website or regularly published newspaper, magazine, or other periodical of general circulation, including an internet or electronic publication, that routinely carries news and commentary of general interest and that publishes a deceptive and fraudulent deepfake if the website or periodical clearly states that the materially deceptive audio or visual media does not accurately represent the speech or conduct of the candidate (Sec. 16, 905(b)(3))
  • Any online publisher or service provider for acts that would be subject to immunity under 47 U.S.C. § 230 (Sec. 16, 905(b)(4))
  • The State Board may not file a civil action against a person exempt from § 16, 905 or a person who seeks to detect, report, prevent, investigate, respond to, or prosecute persons responsible for security breaches, identity theft, fraud, harassment, or other malicious or illegal activity (Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(i))
  • The State Board may not seek damages, court costs, or attorney's fees against a person exempt from § 16, 905 (Sec. 2, 110(c)(3)(ii))
  • The State Administrator may not seek an injunction against an interactive computer service for content disseminated by another person (Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(ii))

Compliance steps

  • Establish a process to monitor and review content for election misinformation, election disinformation, and deepfakes as defined in Sec. 2, 110(a)(2), (3) and Sec. 16, 905(a)(2)
  • Before creating, using, or disseminating any AI-generated image, audio, or video depicting a person in an election context, verify that it does not fall within the prohibited intents and harm requirements of Sec. 16, 905(c)
  • Implement human review and provenance tracking for generative AI outputs to avoid knowing or reckless disregard of materially false information (Sec. 16, 905(c))
  • If content is satire or parody, ensure it clearly qualifies under Sec. 16, 905(b)(1); if it is a broadcast or news publication, provide the required disclosure under Sec. 16, 905(b)(2) or (3)
  • Respond promptly to any correction, injunction, or subpoena from the State Administrator under Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(i)1, 2, 3
  • Maintain records of content creation, dissemination, and any corrective actions to defend against a civil action by the State Board under Sec. 2, 110(c)(2)(ii) and the clear and convincing evidence standard in Sec. 2, 110(c)(4)
  • Train staff on the definitions of election misinformation, election disinformation, and deepfake, and on the criminal penalties in Sec. 16, 905(d)
  • Consult legal counsel regarding the applicability of 47 U.S.C. § 230 immunity and the exemptions in Sec. 16, 905(b) and Sec. 2, 110(c)(1)(ii), (2)(i), (3)(ii)
